design.concept: Mobile "fila de compromissos": a single narrow column that opens on my tasks (quick-filter pills, stacked rows with deadline and status, a thumb-reachable "Nova tarefa" bar). Tapping a task moves to a focused view of that task with its data, checklist, collapsed history and a sticky action bar for the one action that matters for my role. Creating, editing and adjusting the checklist are separate steps, so one thing at a time.

views.purpose: Primary view: my tasks, filter pills, load more, and the Nova tarefa button at the thumb.

The open task: returned-reason note, data card, read-only checklist, collapsed history, and a sticky action bar (main lifecycle action plus a 'Mais ações' menu with return-with-reason and cancel-with-confirmation).
Create a task with stacked fields and an initial checklist; success stays local with a link to the created task.
Edit the task fields, including swapping the assignee; save is disabled until valid and changed.
Mark, reword or add checklist items and save them without changing the task status.

design.decisions: Views use the scene host in scenary mode with back; the host's change handler reloads the list when coming back from creation and discards unsaved edits when leaving edit/checklist. The list uses the responsive data table with three columns (task identity, deadline, status), so no column is hidden at 360px; overdue deadlines are the only text in alarm color, with a plain-word label beside it. No client-side search (the contract has no term query) and no progress bar molecule: the checklist progress arrives as a ready string and is displayed as-is. The page holds no state, so 'Mais ações' and the history are native details disclosures, and cancel is a nested disclosure that names the task before the single danger button. Command feedback is local, inside the sticky bar/panel above the button (success in status colors, failure with the backend message). The returned-reason note is plain markup, not a banner molecule, because the banner reads its slot HTML once and could show stale text. The assignee uses the combobox (alternative) because its keystroke event lets the page call the member search. The deadline uses the date picker, not the shortcut picker, because the shortcuts point to the past. Text inputs listen to input and change with a guard on the custom event detail.
